name: Light Dull Bluish Violet
lede: Light Dull Bluish Violet is a muted light violet from Ridgway's 1912 atlas, filed again by name in the 1955 ISCC-NBS dictionary, built from a three-word modifier chain on plain [[violet]].

sections.title: A modifier chain on Violet
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* carries this swatch on plate XXXVI, hue 57″″, tone b [1]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS dictionary files the exact name "Light Dull Bluish Violet" under block 210, "light violet" [2]. The name stacks three modifiers, light, dull and bluish, onto [[violet]], describing a desaturated, blue-leaning version of the color rather than naming a new source [1].

In our color library its closest neighbor is [[dark-greyish-lavender]], about 3.5 units away and nearly the same color [3]. [[blue-bell]] and [[ontario-violet]] both sit 4.2 units off, more vivid and bluer respectively [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive of 23,781 paintings matches this tone in 48 of them, about 0.2 percent, as photographed, rarer than 59 percent of the named colors we track [4]. It peaks in the 1900s, present in 6 of the 1,674 paintings from that decade, 2.0 times the rate its museums' own baseline would predict [4].

Inside a painting it most often plays a hidden color, in 60 percent of its 25 clearly-ranked appearances [4]. The earliest dated match is 1516, in a painting by Sebastiano del Piombo, 396 years before the name's first 1912 record, so this is a look-alike hue in an old photograph, not proof of the name's age [4]. The archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, and the match is a computed color reading, not a pigment identification [4].
